samples.claim: Shared-ID test accepts both new paths, rejects one rewritten plus one retained old path; asserts InvalidInput and rewrite-required substring. This is multi-fragment coverage for two semantic change categories, not encoding/dictionary variants or physical verification.

samples.claim: Sparse rank test uses offsets 1,63,511,9999 in a 10000-row universe, asserts Sparse, rejects missing zero and checks ranks 0 through 3. It crosses word boundaries without invoking dense representation.

samples.claim: TryFrom creation-version protobuf arm has the same infallible local control flow and allocation/validation boundaries. Separate implementations are needed because protobuf uses distinct oneof types.
samples.review_note: Fresh adjacent last-updated and creation-version implementations each return Inline Arc or Column with no local failure branch. Distinct generated oneof types explain separate impls.

samples.claim: encode dispatches from the configured key_type over unsigned/signed 8/16/32/64; unsupported types return Schema with Debug type. Supported type plus empty input reaches the assertion, whereas unsupported type returns its error without examining the slice. No per-array schema preflight or rollback is added.
samples.review_note: All eight key types and Schema fallback match. Fresh write_typed_array confirms empty assertion precedes first-array access and IO on supported branches, with no common-array validation or rollback.

samples.claim: Invalid-GBO test writes hello global, reads all bytes and decodes footer, then corrupts the FIRST GBO descriptor (schema index0), not user buffer1. Unaligned=(1,0), pastEOF=nextalignmentboundary withsize0, overflow=largest alignedu64 plusone alignment. Overwrites file; arithmetic here is test fixture construction.
samples.review_note: Fresh fixture helper returns user global index1; corrupted bytes begin at the GBO table start, index0. Exact unaligned, next-boundary and overflowing arithmetic and file overwrite match.

samples.claim: test_default_store_returns_but_does_not_persist_etag performs a real ordinary commit through the default external workflow, HEADs the canonical object, compares the returned ETag, and asserts the external record has ETag None. Its next phase changes physical bytes at the same canonical path to test the intended generation-independent external index.
samples.review_note: Ordinary commit, canonical HEAD ETag equality and missing external ETag match. Fresh tail overwrites the same object bytes, asserts a changed ETag and resolves the new physical generation.

samples.claim: Positive-count partial refresh allocates per-row Vec<u64>. Existing Column last-updated metadata requires spilled[fragment.id].last_updated_at or contextual NotSupported; loaded Arc payload is deep-cloned to an owned sequence. Existing Inline decode uses load_sequence().ok(), silently replacing a decode error with prev_version defaults. A decoded/loaded sequence is lazily expanded, truncated to count and padded with prev_version; no length mismatch error. Missing metadata also defaults every row.
samples.review_note: Positive-count branch, mandatory preloaded Column last_updated_at, owned clone, inline .ok() fallback, take/resize truncation-padding and prev_version defaults all match.

samples.claim: entry_size<T> checks TypeId under read lock, recovers poisoned guards with into_inner, then conditionally writes entry.or_insert(contextual accessor). Race-safe insertion does not require holding read and write locks together. All guards are dropped before cache_entry_size(value), permitting custom DeepSizeOf to reenter cache APIs. Registry persists for state lifetime and is not bounded/cleared here. Poison recovery does not clear the poison flag.
samples.review_note: Read guard ends before write guard; both end before custom size calculation. Fresh state definition/constructor and registry usage confirm retained accessors with poison recovery rather than clearing poison.

samples.claim: From<object_store::Error> converts direct NotFound path to Lance NotFound and intentionally drops its original source; every other store error is boxed as IO. From<prost::DecodeError> retains the decode error as boxed IO. Both track caller. Losing the source for direct store NotFound is an explicit exception to general preservation.
samples.review_note: Direct object-store NotFound intentionally discards source; other store errors and prost decode errors use boxed IO. Both conversions carry track_caller.

samples.claim: Option<T> delegates to Some inner children or returns zero for None. The discriminant and inline T storage are left to the parent/default footprint rather than counted again.
samples.review_note: Some delegates children and None returns0; fresh DeepSizeOf default adds size_of_val once, confirming inline Option footprint is not duplicated.
